scope.instruction: https://alfikr.id/ audit web ini, mode debug di django nya juga aktif. bisa lihat sedikit isi di setting ketika debug. selanjutnya cari kerentannannya

agents.task: Assess login/session/JWT-like flows, password/reset behavior if present, rate limits, privilege escalation, workflow/state manipulation, race conditions on contributor/editorial actions. Validate concrete impact and spawn focused validators for candidates.

On the authorized target https://alfikr.id/, use the user-provided low-privilege test credentials (email shahibshahib01@gmail.com, password supplied in parent context) only for non-destructive validation. Log in, determine actual role/permissions, inspect reachable profile/user-management endpoints, and test whether privilege escalation is possible without changing production data. Do not promote the account, alter users/articles, or submit destructive mutations. If a safe read-only proof of missing authorization or mass-assignment is possible, report evidence to parent and spawn a reporting child; otherwise record coverage as no_issue_found or needs_follow_up with precise gap. Handle credentials securely and do not echo them in notes or reports.

File a vulnerability report for confirmed unauthenticated IDOR/BFLA on https://alfikr.id/tulisan/download/<pk>/. Evidence: anonymous GET /tulisan/download/35/ and /36/ returns HTTP 200 application/zip archives containing uploaded DOCX and photo files despite anonymous GET /tulisan/check-download/35/ and /36/ returning HTTP 403 'Status tulisan masih draft.' Include PoC script, impact, CVSS honestly, counterevidence, CWE, and no source code locations (black-box). Parent is agent e987d45f; report only after reviewing this evidence.

Validate suspected IDOR/BFLA on unauthenticated GET /tulisan/download/<pk>/ at https://alfikr.id/. Confirm downloaded archive contents for contributor IDs 33,35,36, whether files are private/non-public, compare check-download behavior and auth/session requirements. If concrete unauthorized disclosure, spawn reporting child; record coverage and report parent.

Assess https://alfikr.id/ specifically for Django debug exposure and information disclosure. Confirm debug pages/settings leakage only, map any traceback/admin/debug endpoints. Record coverage and send evidence; if a concrete vuln is found, spawn a focused validation child per workflow.

Create the formal vulnerability report for the confirmed unauthenticated Django DEBUG information disclosure on https://alfikr.id/. Use validator evidence: GET /save-token/ and /data/json/berita/ return large technical 500 pages exposing Django/Python versions, full traceback/source snippets and paths, BASE_DIR, DB engine/host/name/user, SMTP user, MEDIA_ROOT/STATIC paths, INSTALLED_APPS/MIDDLEWARE; SECRET_KEY/passwords masked. Random invalid path exposes URLconf route inventory. Calibrate Medium (limited restricted config/source disclosure, no raw secrets). Include counterevidence, confidence high, CWE-209 if appropriate, and no code_locations because black-box. File via create_vulnerability_report, then tell parent report ID. Record/update coverage outcome reported. Call get_threat_model first.

Validate the suspected unauthenticated Django DEBUG information disclosure on https://alfikr.id/. Reproduce at least one deterministic 500 route (e.g. /save-token/ or /data/json/berita/), capture what settings/path data is exposed, test whether secrets are masked, and assess severity. This is a validation task only; if confirmed, report back with evidence and ask parent to spawn a reporting agent. Record coverage for the tested routes. Call get_threat_model first.

Using shared threat model and discovered routes, test BOLA/IDOR and broken function-level authorization on article IDs, contributor records, editorial JSON/CRUD/admin routes. Compare unauthenticated and any available sessions; validate concrete unauthorized read/write. If candidate found, spawn validation child; report coverage.

Using my confirmed evidence for https://alfikr.id/penulis/data/json/kontributor/ and public /media/fileTulisan/... downloads, prepare and file the formal vulnerability report. Demonstrate unauthenticated cross-user contributor PII/document disclosure, include counterevidence, calibrated CVSS, PoC code, and no source code locations (black-box). Do not re-test unrelated endpoints. Record coverage if needed and report the vuln ID to me/parent.

Independently validate unauthenticated GET /penulis/data/json/kontributor/ on https://alfikr.id/. Confirm whether response contains real contributor PII (names, phone, email, address, file paths), assess scope and sensitivity, test auth/method controls, and if confirmed spawn a reporting child to file the formal vulnerability report. Record/update coverage.

Independently validate suspected missing authorization on https://alfikr.id/ JSON article state endpoints `/edit/berita/publish/` and `/edit/berita/takedown/`. Use unauthenticated fresh session, POST JSON with an existing article ID, verify before/after public visibility and persistence. If confirmed, spawn a reporting child (reporting must file complete PoC-backed report; black-box no code fix). Record coverage.

Using confirmed PoC from parent: unauthenticated session obtains CSRF token from `/redaksi/login/`, then POST JSON `{id:<public article id>}` to `/edit/berita/takedown/` and `/edit/berita/publish/`; both return status true and article disappears/reappears in `/cari/berita/terbaru/json/`. File one black-box vulnerability report for missing function-level authorization (CSRF is not auth), with concrete Python PoC, CVSS honest (likely High for unauthorized editorial modification/availability), counterevidence and severity change condition. Do not test unrelated issues.

Perform comprehensive black-box reconnaissance and attack-surface mapping for https://alfikr.id/: subdomains, ports, technologies, endpoints, parameters, forms, JS/routes. Do not deep exploit. Record coverage and shared notes; report discovered inventory to parent.

URLs: - https://alfikr.id/

Test all mapped input surfaces on https://alfikr.id/ for SQL injection: search POST/JSON parameters, filters, path IDs/slugs, tags and editorial data endpoints. Use bounded automated sprays and validate true DB effects; spawn validation child for any candidate and record coverage.

Assess mapped upload, JSON, token, contributor, and editorial endpoints for SSRF, XXE, command/template injection, deserialization or RCE. First identify actual parser/fetch sinks via behavior; validate only concrete impact and spawn validators for candidates.

Confirmed stored XSS via unauthenticated contributor SVG upload. File one vulnerability report using create_vulnerability_report, include complete PoC, counterevidence, CVSS, and no source code locations (black-box). Target https://alfikr.id/, endpoint POST /create/tulisan/kontributor/ and GET /media/fileTulisan/exec7811.svg. Use evidence that Chrome execution set documentElement[data-pwned]='yes'. Avoid duplicate with any existing stored XSS report if dedupe rejects. Call agent_finish after filing.

Validate suspected stored XSS from unauthenticated contributor upload: arbitrary SVG file accepted and served at /media/fileTulisan/<name> image/svg+xml with script intact. Demonstrate browser execution and impact if possible; record coverage; if confirmed spawn reporting child per workflow.

Validate suspected stored XSS from unauthenticated POST /create/tulisan/kontributor/ fields (nama/mediaSosial/alamat/deskripsiDiri). Payload <svg/onload=alert(1)> was accepted and appears in /penulis/data/json/kontributor/ JSON as id 69. Determine whether any reachable public/editorial rendering executes it, using browser or endpoint behavior. If confirmed, spawn reporting child; otherwise document specific control/gap and record coverage.

Focus exclusively on /create/tulisan/kontributor/ multipart upload and any file-serving/download paths for unrestricted upload, path traversal/LFI, MIME/extension bypass, and stored execution/XSS. Validate impact, spawn validator if candidate, record coverage.

Validate candidate stored XSS/unrestricted upload on https://alfikr.id/ POST /create/tulisan/kontributor/ and GET /media/fileTulisan/<uploaded-name>. Reproduce upload of HTML/SVG via multipart with valid image, confirm browser script execution and headers, test path traversal filename if feasible. If confirmed, spawn a nested Upload XSS Reporting agent; otherwise record closure. Do not overlap general XSS surfaces.

Independently crawl and enumerate the public web application at https://alfikr.id/ using bounded crawling and content discovery, focusing APIs, forms, auth flows, uploads, GraphQL, and hidden paths. No exploit spraying yet. Record coverage and provide endpoint inventory.

Test public search, contributor submission, article/detail, token and editorial forms for reflected/stored/DOM XSS and CSRF bypasses. Use automated payload sprays and browser validation where needed; spawn separate validation child per confirmed candidate and record coverage.

caveats: 3 agent(s) did not finish cleanly (Auth Business Logic Tester, Root Agent, Upload Path Tester); any surface they held is under-covered.

entries.risk_area: Django DEBUG traceback and settings information disclosure
entries.evidence: Independent validation reproduced unauthenticated HTTP 500 Django technical pages on the listed routes. Report `vuln-0001` documents the confirmed DEBUG=True traceback, source-path, settings, and route-inventory disclosure; secrets were masked.

entries.risk_area: Exposed admin/debug/observability and API documentation endpoints
entries.evidence: Forced browsing returned generic Django 404 pages for all listed paths; no admin login, debug toolbar, metrics, health, Swagger, or OpenAPI interface was reachable at these candidate locations.

entries.surface: Public HTML and dynamic routes on https://alfikr.id/
entries.risk_area: Attack-surface enumeration (APIs, forms, auth, uploads, GraphQL, hidden paths)
entries.evidence: Bounded Katana/Gospider crawl, HTML/script extraction, and 46-path ffuf discovery identified public pages, login/submission forms, JSON routes, article/category routes, media/static assets, and Firebase service worker; no GraphQL/OpenAPI/admin API endpoint was found in the tested inventory.

entries.risk_area: Endpoint behavior and method/auth surface mapping
entries.evidence: GET latest JSON is publicly accessible; POST search is CSRF-protected (GET returns 403); filter and save-token GET requests generate Django 500 debug responses. Their security impact and input handling require dedicated validation.

Report `vuln-0001` filed after independent reproduction of unauthenticated `GET /save-token/` HTTP 500 (~64KB) exposing DEBUG=True, traceback/source paths, runtime and configuration metadata; sensitive secret fields were masked.
Later reporting independently reproduced the same unauthenticated DEBUG 500 on `/data/json/berita/`; this surface is covered by `vuln-0001`.
Later reporting independently reproduced the DEBUG 404 route-inventory disclosure; this surface is covered by `vuln-0001`.

entries.risk_area: debug information disclosure / exposed route and source paths
entries.evidence: Dedicated validation and report `vuln-0001` confirmed DEBUG 404/500 disclosure on invalid paths and exposed routes.

Unauthenticated GET returns three contributor records containing names, phone numbers, email addresses, physical addresses, social handles, workflow statuses, editor names, and uploaded file paths; each tested file path is downloadable anonymously as a DOCX. Formal report vuln-0002 filed.
Several data/statistics endpoints return 200 without authentication; no cross-account object test performed during reconnaissance.

entries.surface: DNS, certificate, HTTP(S), and TCP service inventory for alfikr.id
entries.evidence: Apex resolves to 36.92.8.230; CT/subfinder found no additional subdomains; ports 80, 443, and 2000 are open, with HTTPS identified as nginx-fronted Django.

entries.surface: Django admin and editorial hidden routes (/admin/alfikr/*, /redaksi/dashboard/, /tambah/berita/, /edit/berita/*, /hapus/berita/json/, /data/json/berita/)
entries.evidence: Caido sitemap and direct baseline requests identify admin login (200), admin root redirect (302), and multiple editorial/data routes returning 302/403/405/500. No credentials were available to determine post-auth behavior or authorization boundaries.

entries.surface: Django debug error pages on malformed/invalid routes
entries.evidence: Dedicated DEBUG validation and report `vuln-0001` confirmed the listed malformed routes leak traceback, versions, source paths, and configuration metadata.

entries.risk_area: Django DEBUG traceback and settings information disclosure
entries.evidence: Independent validator reproduced HTTP 500 (64,842-byte technical page) unauthenticated; page exposes JSONDecodeError traceback/source at `berita.views.save_token` line 132, Django 5.2.8/Python 3.12.10, `/home/web2` paths, DB/SMTP metadata, middleware/apps, and DEBUG=True. Secrets are masked.

entries.risk_area: Django DEBUG traceback and settings information disclosure
entries.evidence: Independent validator reproduced HTTP 500 (52,621-byte technical page) unauthenticated with `AttributeError` traceback at `berita/views.py:1341` and same settings/environment disclosure; secrets masked.

entries.risk_area: Django DEBUG URLconf and route inventory disclosure
entries.evidence: Unauthenticated Django debug 404 page exposes `DEBUG=True`, project URLconf `Alfikr.urls`, and a complete route inventory including `/admin/alfikr/`, `/redaksi/`, data, management, upload, and download paths.
Dedicated validation confirmed these unauthenticated 500 responses are instances of the reported DEBUG disclosure in `vuln-0001`.
Nmap top-100 identified TCP/2000 open, but service/version/banner enrichment timed out; service ownership and security impact remain unconfirmed.

Anonymous GET returns 200 JSON containing contributor names, phone numbers, email addresses, physical addresses, social handles, statuses, editor names, and uploaded file paths; no authentication or session required. Reporting child is filing formal vulnerability report.

Anonymous GET to /media/fileTulisan/Opini_Banjir_Jember.docx returns 200 DOCX (14,626 bytes) with public caching; document contains unpublished contributor submission and identity context. Filename is disclosed by the unauthenticated contributor endpoint.
Unauthenticated request returns contributor names, phone numbers, email addresses, physical addresses, submission file paths and statuses for IDs 33, 35, 36.
Independent validator confirmed anonymous ZIP downloads for draft IDs despite `/tulisan/check-download/` returning 403; covered by `vuln-0003`.

entries.risk_area: IDOR/BOLA and broken function-level authorization on contributor submission downloads
entries.evidence: Unauthenticated GET requests for IDs 35 and 36 return HTTP 200 ZIP archives containing uploaded DOCX and JPEG files, while unauthenticated GET /tulisan/check-download/35/ and /36/ returns HTTP 403 with 'Status tulisan masih draft.' The direct download bypasses the status gate; ID 33 also downloads 200.
Enumerated IDs 1750-1840; existing articles are intentionally public, while nonexistent IDs redirect to homepage. No private object distinction observed.

Unauthenticated GET/POST probes to CRUD/admin endpoints either redirect to /redaksi/dashboard/ or return 500 due missing required data; publish/update actions redirect and did not mutate state. No unauthorized state change demonstrated.

entries.risk_area: Authorization gate consistency for contributor draft downloads
entries.evidence: Unauthenticated requests to IDs 35 and 36 return HTTP 403 JSON `{"status": false, "message": "Status tulisan masih draft."}`; this status gate itself blocks draft downloads, although the sibling direct-download route bypasses it.

entries.risk_area: IDOR / broken object-level authorization on contributor archives
entries.evidence: Anonymous GET requests for IDs 35 and 36 returned HTTP 200 application/zip archives containing DOCX and photo files, while check-download for both IDs returned 403 draft-status responses; reported as vuln-0003.
For draft contributor IDs 35 and 36, check-download endpoint enforces 403 status draft, but direct download endpoint returns 200 ZIP with DOCX and photo, bypassing workflow gate.
Unauthenticated submission without token or with invalid token returned HTTP 403; valid same-origin token accepted. Django CSRF middleware blocks missing/foreign Origin requests.
Requests without or with invalid `csrfmiddlewaretoken` returned HTTP 403; valid token request reached application and returned normal login JSON.
JSON POST without token returned 403, foreign Origin returned 403, and same-origin request with current `X-CSRFToken` succeeded. Endpoint enforces CSRF.

entries.risk_area: SSRF / XXE / RCE via uploaded documents
entries.evidence: Uploaded XML/SVG/PHP and traversal-named files are stored and served, but no server-side parser, URL fetch, or code execution was observed; PHP content served as octet-stream rather than executed. SVG script handling remains delegated to XSS validation.

entries.risk_area: Unrestricted file upload / stored XSS / server-side execution
entries.evidence: Confirmed arbitrary file upload and stored XSS: unauthenticated multipart submission accepts attacker-controlled HTML/SVG/JS despite UI extension restrictions, stores under `/media/fileTulisan/`, and serves inline with attacker MIME/body absent `Content-Disposition` and `X-Content-Type-Options`. Uploaded HTML executed JavaScript in a browser; sibling validation/reporting filed this root cause as `vuln-0005`. Filename traversal attempts were normalized and did not demonstrate path escape.
Endpoint only calls JSON parsing and stores `token` via ORM get_or_create; URL/gopher strings are accepted as opaque values and no outbound request or execution occurred.
Sprayed marker and SVG payloads in form and JSON search parameters; HTML responses did not contain markers and JSON responses returned fixed article records without reflection.
These search/filter handlers expose ORM query and template/JSON response errors but accept no URL/XML/document input and showed no execution or server-side fetch primitive.

Path payloads were either HTML-escaped in Django DEBUG 404 pages or URL-encoded in article share links; no attacker markup appeared in executable HTML context. Category payload redirected to homepage.

Unauthenticated requests reach Django views and fail on AnonymousUser attributes; no attacker-controlled URL/XML or command sink is present in observed behavior. Authenticated editorial credentials were unavailable for deeper parser testing.

Attacker-controlled contributor fields are stored verbatim and exposed unauthenticated as JSON (id 69). Rendering context in authenticated editorial dashboard could not be reached because dashboard consistently returns 500/redirects without credentials; execution impact remains unconfirmed.

Page JavaScript assigns API-controlled `title`, `category`, and `img` values directly into `innerHTML` templates. Public JSON currently contains trusted article data, but ability for an attacker to alter article fields was not established.

Homepage JavaScript renders `title`, `category`, and `img` from `/filter/terpopuler/berita/` into `innerHTML` without visible escaping. Endpoint currently errors for some filters and attacker ability to modify article data was not confirmed.

Obtained the public CSRF token and tested benign, quote, tautology, contradiction, comment, and SLEEP payloads in `cari`, `tahun`, and `bulan`; responses remained application HTML with no SQL errors, predicate effects, or repeatable timing shift.

With a valid CSRF token, sprayed all JSON/form fields using quotes, tautologies, contradictions, comments, and SLEEP variants; normal searches returned expected result counts or 'not found', with no SQL exception or reliable timing oracle.

All tested filter values, including quotes, tautologies, and SLEEP strings, produced the same Django TypeError (`NoneType` not iterable) at the application lookup path; no SQL parser error, differential result, or repeatable delay was observed.

Tested valid article ID 1830 with normal, quote, tautology, comment, and SLEEP slug variants; route returned the same article page without SQL error or repeatable timing oracle. Non-integer ID payloads are rejected by Django URL typing with 404.

Valid page values returned normal HTML; quote, tautology, and SLEEP payloads in integer page segments were rejected with 404 by Django URL converters, and invalid numeric IDs only triggered a generic debug application exception.

entries.surface: Unauthenticated contributor submission fields (id=69) and public contributor/detail routes
entries.evidence: POSTed SVG payloads in `nama`, `mediaSosial`, `alamat`, and `deskripsiDiri`; `/penulis/data/json/kontributor/` returns them verbatim as `application/json` (non-executable). `/penulis/kontributor/` and `/detail/tulisan/kontributor/69/` redirect unauthenticated requests to `/redaksi/dashboard/`, so authenticated editorial templates that may render these fields could not be reached or ruled out without valid editor credentials.

Route consistently raises a `NoneType.tags` exception for tested tags and IDs, preventing a clean result oracle; no SQL parser error was seen, but the underlying query behavior cannot be fully confirmed without source or a known existing tag/article combination.

entries.risk_area: Missing function-level authorization / business logic state manipulation
entries.evidence: Unauthenticated fresh session with a valid CSRF token can POST JSON `{id:1830}`; both endpoints return `{"status": true}` and takedown removes the article from `/cari/berita/terbaru/json/`, while publish restores it.

Valid-CSRF wrong-email attempts consistently reveal `Email belum terdaftar!` versus known blocked email `Akun Anda telah diblokir`; twelve rapid attempts showed no throttling or lockout, but no valid account was available to prove credential guessing or account takeover impact.
IDOR validator and reporter confirmed draft archive downloads bypass the companion authorization check; covered by `vuln-0003`.

entries.risk_area: Business logic / duplicate submission and workflow integrity
entries.evidence: Public users can submit unlimited contributor records with valid CSRF; repeated identical submissions each returned success and created new draft records. No deduplication or per-identity rate limit was observed, but direct operational impact (storage exhaustion or editorial queue abuse) was not quantified.
Service worker is static Firebase messaging code; no attacker-controlled input or dynamic HTML sinks observed.

entries.risk_area: Stored XSS via uploaded active content
entries.evidence: Dedicated validator and report `vuln-0005` confirmed browser execution from uploaded SVG served inline.

entries.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization / unauthorized editorial state change
entries.evidence: Unauthenticated session with only a CSRF token successfully hid and restored an arbitrary public article; report vuln-0004 filed with reproduction and remediation.

Unauthenticated session obtains csrftoken from /redaksi/login/ and POSTs JSON {"id":1829}; both endpoints return status:true. Subsequent authenticated-free search JSON shows article 1829 disappears after takedown and reappears after publish, proving durable public visibility mutation.

entries.risk_area: Stored XSS via unrestricted SVG upload
entries.evidence: Unauthenticated multipart submission accepted an SVG payload when filename was .svg (or arbitrary content with .docx); GET returned 200 image/svg+xml with script intact. Chromium execution was verified: opening /media/fileTulisan/exec7811.svg set documentElement[data-pwned] to yes.
Unauthenticated multipart upload accepted an SVG and served it inline as image/svg+xml; Chrome execution set documentElement[data-pwned]='yes'. Report vuln-0005 filed.

entries.risk_area: Stored XSS via arbitrary HTML upload
entries.evidence: Independent reproduction: authenticated only by CSRF token, multipart accepted `unique7744.html` with HTML MIME and returned JSON status true. Public GET served exact script as `text/html` without `Content-Disposition` or `X-Content-Type-Options`; Chromium executed it (document title changed to `XSS_EXEC`). Existing report/coverage entries cover the same root cause; no duplicate filed.

A `.php` payload was accepted and publicly served, but GET returned the literal PHP source as `application/octet-stream`; no interpreter execution or transformed output occurred. This specific upload-serving path is static-only for PHP content.

entries.risk_area: Server-side code execution from uploaded scripts and extension bypasses
entries.evidence: Uploaded `.php`, `.phtml`, `.cgi`, `.py`, and double-extension canaries; retrieval either returned 404 or static source/octet-stream. The `.php` canary response contained literal PHP source (`<?php echo "RCE_MARKER_7744"; ?>`), demonstrating no interpreter execution.

entries.evidence: The deployed target exposes no source repository to trace template/deserialization/command sinks; upload retrieval tests only established static serving and do not cover privileged editorial processing paths.
